headline: VW halts mega-casting; Mercedes to use 75% recycled aluminium from 2027

summary.text: Volkswagen has halted mega-casting and dropped the in-house Wolfsburg foundry for SSP models, which may keep mid-size structural castings with external die casters like Lindner.
Mercedes will use aluminium with 75% recycled content from 2027, which means near-term demand for scrap-tolerant secondary alloys in Lindner's structural parts.
ZEISS INRADIA 3D brings industrial tomography to the production line, and it could let Lindner move porosity checks inline without losing cycle time.

actions.text: Sales lead: contact VW purchasing about SSP shock tower and frame sourcing, and check whether the gigacasting halt opens volume for Lindner.
Technical lead: assess whether Lindner's current alloys and suppliers can deliver 75% recycled content, and prepare a position for Mercedes.
Quality manager: request ZEISS INRADIA 3D specifications and a sample-part trial to test inline use against current X-ray inspection.

items.title: Volkswagen halts mega-casting as automakers embrace pragmatism
items.reason: VW halting mega-casting signals OEMs retreating from in-house gigacasting, easing a key threat to Lindner's shock tower and frame volumes.
